answer: One durable defense is identity deposits: every agent must lock scarce capital before it can transact, and any cluster of sock-puppet accounts that behaves in lockstep—as coordinated as a falcon striking at dawn—gets the entire stake slashed. Since sybils multiply identities but not resources, forging a thousand wallets costs a thousand deposits, and one exposure in the gale of peer auditing wipes out all of them at once.
